issues.summary: Blueprint internally inconsistent about execution-phase artifact template count (5 vs 7); Change Impact Map omits 2 of 5 AC-FR-7-c floor items

evidence.quote_paraphrase: Lists 5 templates: per-task-execution-result, phase-quality-report, quality-reconciliation-log, state-transitions-log-entry-schema, pipeline-run-summary. Does NOT include frontmatter-validation-report or execution-reconciliation-log.

Claims '5 execution-phase artifact templates (the FR-7-c floor: per-task-execution-result, phase-quality-report, quality-reconciliation-log, frontmatter-validation-report, execution-reconciliation-log) plus 2 beyond floor (state-transitions-log-entry-schema, pipeline-run-summary)' — i.e., 7 templates total.
Says '5 execution-phase artifact types listed in FR-7-c floor plus the 2 introduced beyond the floor' = 7 total.
Enumerates 5 execution-phase artifacts (same as Change Impact Map; missing frontmatter-validation-report and execution-reconciliation-log).
Names 5 floor items: per-task execution log; phase-quality report; quality-reconciliation log (per cycle); frontmatter-validation report; execution-reconciliation log.

issues.impact: The Change Impact Map is the actionable artifact for Plan-stage task generation. A Plan author following the Map alone will create 5 template tasks and miss 2 floor items, leaving the feature out of conformance with AC-FR-7-c. This is precisely the 'missing artifacts at packaging time' failure mode the feature was designed to eliminate.
issues.recommended_resolution: Reconcile the count in one direction: either (a) treat frontmatter-validation-report and execution-reconciliation-log as scope (add them to the Change Impact Map and ADR-0033's enumeration), or (b) document explicit dispositions for the two missing items (e.g., 'frontmatter-validation-report' = JSON output of validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py, no template required because not a pair-pattern artifact; 'execution-reconciliation-log' = same as quality-reconciliation-log under a different name). Whichever direction is chosen, all four documents (Change Impact Map, AC traceability at line 1973, ADR-0032 Change 5, ADR-0033 Context enumeration) must agree.

issues.summary: ADR-0034 makes a factual claim about ADR-0021's content that is not supported by ADR-0021's actual text

evidence.quote_paraphrase: Says 'ADR-0021 inherits and applies the cap (referencing it in the planning-phase architecture context); ADR-0017 defines it.' Decision: 'ADR-0021 inherits and applies the cap in the planning-phase architecture context; ADR-0017 defines it.'

grep for '4-cycle' / '4 cycle' / 'cycle cap' / 'reconciliation cap' in ADR-0021 returns zero matches. The only cap referenced in ADR-0021 is the ≤6 parallel external-research cap (line 85, attributed to ADR-0006) — unrelated to the 4-cycle reconciliation cap.
States 'Iteration cap: 4 cycles (matching the pipeline's broader fixed-point iteration discipline from blueprint v3 §3.7).' This is the only ADR text that names '4 cycles' explicitly.
Multiple repetitions of the unsupported credit to ADR-0021 as canonical home for the planning-side reconciliation budget. This is the documentary mis-credit ADR-0034 is meant to correct.

issues.impact: ADR-0034 is the corrective document; future readers will follow it to understand the canonical ownership of the 4-cycle cap. The corrective document itself contains an attribution error about ADR-0021's actual content. Operationally the decision (cite ADR-0017 going forward) is correct, but the factual framing 'ADR-0021 inherits and applies' is not grounded in ADR-0021's text and risks propagating a different misunderstanding (i.e., that ADR-0021 contains material on the cap, when it doesn't).
issues.recommended_resolution: Revise ADR-0034's Context and Decision sections to drop the 'ADR-0021 inherits and applies the cap' framing. Suggested replacement: 'The actual canonical home is ADR-0017, which introduces the 4-cycle reconciliation cap as part of the document-reviewer flow. ADR-0021 (discovery-phase architecture) does NOT in fact reference or apply this cap — its appearance in PRD v1.1.0 Dependencies as the canonical home is an attribution error that this ADR corrects.' Note also that ADR-0017's own text traces the cap further back to 'blueprint v3 §3.7' (line 155), which is the deepest provenance available — worth a one-sentence footnote for completeness but not strictly required for the corrective purpose.

issues.summary: Contract 4 dispatch matrix scope_deviations row has dynamic dispatch target ('the agent whose deviation was unsurfaced') without a procedure for identifying that agent

evidence.quote_paraphrase: Row: 'scope_deviations (ADR-0033 addition) | scope-deviation-scan | the agent whose deviation was unsurfaced | deviation context + scope-deviation finding'. The dispatch target is dynamic; no procedure given for resolving it to a concrete agent.

issues.impact: execute-finalize-reconciler needs to dispatch findings to a concrete agent. 'The agent whose deviation was unsurfaced' is the answer but requires a deterministic resolution procedure (e.g., inspect surfacing-location chain: if the deviation should have been in per-task-execution-result, the responsible agent is the code-producer or quality-handler whose return contract was supposed to include the scope_deviations field). Without this procedure, runtime dispatch becomes ambiguous.
issues.recommended_resolution: Add to the dispatch-matrix surrounding prose (or to ADR-0033) the resolution procedure: 'For scope_deviations findings, the reconciler resolves dispatch target by walking the surfacing-location chain — the artifact where the deviation should have surfaced names the agent in its authoring-frontmatter; that agent is the dispatch target. Fallback: if the surfacing-location chain is ambiguous, escalate to user per AC-FR-10-c.'
